text.p: Gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Thursday that it expected lower earnings in the year to June 30, 1997.
When asked if Newcrest was expected to post a lower year result, managing director John Quinn told reporters: "Yes, absolutely." Quinn did not elaborate.
Newcrest earlier announced a half year pre-tax profit of A$8.5 million, down from A$21.7 million a year ago.

Newcrest had a 1995/96 (July-June) net profit of A$20.81 million, compared with A$66.23 million a year earlier, although this figure consisted of 18 months as the company changed its balance date from December 31.
Operating profit fell to A$27.13 million from A$104.87 million.

Quinn said second half earnings would continue to be affected by lower grades and a short-term closure at the company's main mine, Telfer, in Western Australia, but the total impact on the full year result remained to be seen.

"The disruption to the Telfer operation by the abnormal rain ... has hit. Until we are able to know when we can reopen and resupply Telfer and restart it we won't know what the severity of that impact is," he said.
